business_scope.primary_industry_name: Self-Insurance Risk Underwriting for Multinational Enterprise Groups

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Free Trade Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the United States of America (KORUS FTA)
Free Trade Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the People's Republic of China
Free Trade Agreement between the Government of the Republic of Korea and the Government of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam
Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement between the Republic of Korea and the Republic of Indonesia
Convention between the Republic of Korea and the Republic of Singapore for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 16261, as amended, Articles 3 and 4; Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, Presidential Decree No. 33233; Commercial Act Articles 289, 292, 330, 332, 369 and 376; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality, Act No. 15516; Foreign Investment Promotion Act; Insurance Business Act Articles 4 and 9; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) Guidelines on Beneficial Owner Identification and Sanctions Screening. Korea maintains no public beneficial ownership register; UBO data reported by financial institutions is available to KoFIU and competent authorities only.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner and intermediate corporate entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Companies Registry or Corporate Registrar in the UBO's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the origin jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention member: notarize or authenticate the certificate and attach an Apostille issued by that state's competent authority. If the origin jurisdiction is not an Apostille member: notarize, authenticate through the origin jurisdiction's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize through the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; never chain them sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Active Status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies, Secretary of State, or equivalent corporate registry in each UBO's corporate domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille Convention states: notarize and apostille through the state of issue, with no additional Korean consular step. For non-Apostille states: notarize, secure foreign Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then Korean consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization must never be combined in one chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing Korean Chusik Hoesa formation and captive reinsurance license application
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate UBO or shareholder entity, duly certified and notarized
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille route: board-certified copy notarized and apostilled by the origin state's competent authority. Consular route: board-certified copy notarized, authenticated by the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The two routes are mutually exclusive and cannot be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Charter / Bylaws of each corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official corporate registry or notary public in the origin jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille Convention jurisdictions: certified copy notarized and apostilled. Non-member jurisdictions: certified copy notarized, authenticated by the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives, not sequential steps.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter regarding UBO source of funds and financial standing
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Primary regulated commercial bank of each UBO or beneficiary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Apostille states: bank officer-signed letter notarized and apostilled. For non-Apostille states: letter notarized, authenticated by the origin state's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Never attach both an Apostille and a consular legalization to the same instrument.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory protocol: verify identity with certified identity documents; screen all UBOs, directors, officers, and license applicants against PEP lists maintained by the Financial Services Commission/FSS and FATF-recommended categories of domestic and foreign prominent public functions, including family and close associates; screen against UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions, and Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act designations; perform ongoing real-time screening on names, aliases, passports, and adverse media; trigger enhanced due diligence upon any match, jurisdiction-high-risk flag, or negative news; retain evidence for at least five years under KoFIU rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registry Office (IROS) - Company Name Reservation service (https://www.iros.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in Hangul (Korean script); a non-Korean name may appear only in parentheses after the Hangul name and cannot replace the registered Hangul name. Phonetic transliterations must follow the Korean pronunciation standards of the National Institute of Korean Language. Under Commercial Act Article 18 and the Commercial Registration Rules, a company name is composed in four tiers: territorial or divisional indicator, distinctive trading name, business-object or industry descriptor, and Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation) legal-form suffix. Identical or confusingly similar

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended) - primary companies statute. Applicable sections include Article 288 (promoters), Article 289 (contents of the articles of incorporation), Article 295 (payment of subscription price by promoters at incorporation), Article 316 (certificate of paid-in capital), Article 317 (registration of incorporation of a stock company), and Articles 382 through 408 (board of directors and statutory officers). Also relevant: Insurance Business Act of the Republic of Korea, Article 4 (permission for insurance business including reinsurance), Article 5 (capital requirements), and Article 7 (business plan); Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 5 and 6 (foreign investment report).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court having jurisdiction over the corporation's registered office in the Republic of Korea; electronic filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Center (IROS); post-registration tax registration with the National Tax Service through Hometax.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa) under Article 317 of the Commercial Act, accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation and a bank deposit balance certificate evidencing full payment of the subscription price.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Commercial Act for a Chusik Hoesa; there is no statutory minimum paid-in capital and promoters may set the capital amount freely in the Articles. However, before court registration, the full subscription price must be deposited into a bank account opened in the name of the company being formed, and the bank must issue a deposit balance certificate. No blocked escrow account is required for a non-public company at incorporation. For captive reinsurance authorization, the Financial Services Commission may impose a prudential minimum paid-in capital or guaranty deposit requirement under the Insurance Business Act as a separate licensing condition.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF THE COMPANY (CHUSIK HOESA) UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. AT A MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COMPANY DULY CONVENED AND HELD AT THE REGISTERED OFFICE ON THE DATE SET FORTH BELOW, WITH A QUORUM OF DIRECTORS PRESENT AND ACTING THROUGHOUT, THE FOLLOWING RESOLUTIONS WERE PROPOSED, CONSIDERED, AND UNANIMOUSLY ADOPTED. 1. CONFIRMATION OF INCORPORATION. THE BOARD NOTED AND RATIFIED THE CERTIFICATE OF INCORPORATION ISSUED BY THE COMPETENT DISTRICT COURT REGISTRY AND CONFIRMED THE INITIAL CAPITAL STRUCTURE SUBSCRIBED BY THE PROMOTERS. 2. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT. RESOLVED, THAT THE ISSUANCE AND ALLOTMENT OF THE SHARES OF THE COMPANY, AT THE PAR VALUE STATED IN THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION, TO THE PERSONS IDENTIFIED IN THE SUBSCRIPTION SCHEDULE BE AND IS HEREBY RATIFIED AND CONFIRMED; AND RESOLVED FURTHER, THAT THE CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER AND CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER ARE AUTHORIZED TO ISSUE SHARE CERTIFICATES, TO UPDATE THE SHAREHOLDER LEDGER, AND TO RECORD THE ALLOTMENT IN ALL STATUTORY BOOKS AND REGISTERS. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, THAT THE COMPANY SHALL MAINTAIN ITS PRINCIPAL CORPORATE, OPERATING, AND UNDERWRITING RESERVE ACCOUNTS AT ONE OR MORE BANKS LOCATED IN THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA; THAT THE AUTHORIZED SIGNATORIES FOR ACCOUNT OPENING, WIRE TRANSFERS, SWIFT PAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS, AND RESERVE TRANSACTIONS SHALL BE THE PERSONS APPOINTED BY THE BOARD; THAT THE BANKS ARE AUTHORIZED TO ACT ON ANY TWO SIGNATORIES IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE SIGNATURE CARD; AND THAT NO ACCOUNT SHALL BE CLOSED OR DISMANTLED WITHOUT PRIOR BOARD APPROVAL. 4. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, THAT THE REGISTERED OFFICE OF THE COMPANY SHALL BE AT THE ADDRESS STATED IN THE ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION, AND THAT THE COMPANY IS AUTHORIZED TO LEASE OR OCCUPY THE PREMISES, TO DISPLAY THE CORPORATE NAMEPLATE, AND TO FILE ALL NOTIFICATIONS WITH THE DISTRICT COURT AND THE NATIONAL TAX SERVICE. 5. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, THAT A REPRESENTATIVE DIRECTOR, A CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER, AND A COMPLIANCE OFFICER ARE APPOINTED, EACH TO SERVE UNTIL THE NEXT ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING, WITH FULL AUTHORITY TO EXECUTE ALL DOCUMENTS, TO MAKE REGULATORY FILINGS WITH THE FINANCIAL SERVICES COMMISSION AND THE FINANCIAL SUPERVISORY SERVICE, AND TO ADMINISTER THE CAPTIVE REINSURANCE AUTHORIZATION PROCESS. 6. REGULATORY AND TAX AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, THAT THE OFFICERS ARE AUTHORIZED TO REGISTER THE COMPANY WITH THE NATIONAL TAX SERVICE, TO OBTAIN THE BUSINESS REGISTRATION CERTIFICATE, TO FILE THE FOREIGN INVESTMENT REPORT WITH KOTRA OR AN AUTHORIZED FOREIGN EXCHANGE BANK, AND TO EXECUTE ANY CONSENTS OR DECLARATIONS REQUIRED BY LAW. 7. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, THAT ANY ONE DIRECTOR OR OFFICER SHALL HAVE FULL POWER TO TAKE ALL LAWFUL STEPS, TO PAY ALL FEES AND TAXES, TO NOTARIZE DOCUMENTS, TO CURE ANY ADMINISTRATIVE OBJECTION, AND TO CARRY OUT THESE RESOLUTIONS. THE FOREGOING RESOLUTIONS WERE UNANIMOUSLY ADOPTED AND RECORDED.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Report and Legal Name Clearance for Non-Resident Shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance via KOTRA Invest Korea and authorized foreign exchange banks in the Republic of Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before incorporation, each non-resident investor must file a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The report is submitted using the prescribed form to the authorized Korean foreign exchange bank or to KOTRA (Invest Korea). The report must identify the investor, proposed investment amount, shareholding ratio, and business scope of the captive reinsurance SPV. Simultaneously, conduct a corporate name search in the Korean Court Registration System to confirm that no identical trade name exists. Upon filing, the bank issues a certificate of foreign exchange bank evidencing the report, which must be kept for subsequent business registration and cash remittance. If the report is incomplete, the investor may amend and resubmit within one month without penalty.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Report Form prescribed under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
Investor identity documents, passport or corporate certificate, apostilled or consular legalized
Power of attorney if an agent is appointed
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Corporate name-search confirmation from the court registry
Bank account opening documentation for remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment report is rejected or queried, the applicant should amend the form and resubmit through the same authorized bank or KOTRA within 30 days; after cure, the certificate is reissued. Failure to cure does not invalidate the later court registration, but it prevents lawful inward remittance for subscription payment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Deposit of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean notary public commissioned under the Notary Public Act, and the recipient Korean bank maintaining the company's capital deposit account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must execute the Articles of Incorporation before a notary public. The Articles must include all statutory matters: corporate name, business purpose (captive reinsurance), total authorized shares, shares issued at incorporation, par value, registered office address, method of public notice, and promoter names and addresses. Each promoter must sign, and the notary certifies the subscription. The share capital must be deposited into a purpose account opened in the name of the company being formed at a Korean bank; the bank deposit balance certificate is required. For a Chusik Hoesa with no minimum capital, the paid-in amount is determined in the Articles. No blocked escrow is required at this stage. The notarial instrument and balance certificate are prerequisites to court registration.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Notarization application form
Promoter identity documents and certified seals
Bank deposit balance certificate for the share subscription
Foreign investment report certificate, if foreign investors are present
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or bank flags deficiencies, amend the Articles, re-execute signatures, or complete the unpaid subscription amount and obtain a corrected deposit balance certificate; no registration may proceed until the notarial certificate and balance certificate are valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of Incorporation with the District Court Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing through the Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Center (IROS).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration of incorporation under Article 317 of the Commercial Act to the district court registry within two weeks after the share capital has been fully paid. The application must include the incorporation registration form, notarized Articles, notarial certificate, bank balance certificate, consent forms of the directors and representative director, certified seal impressions, proof of registered office, and the foreign investment report certificate. The court reviews the filing for statutory compliance and issues the corporate registration certificate. Legal existence begins on the registration date. Registration tax and local education surtax are assessed on paid-in capital and must be paid before registration is entered. After issuance, obtain certified corporate registration extracts and complete the corporate seal register.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation under Article 317 of the Commercial Act
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of share subscription and payment
Bank deposit balance certificate
Consent forms of directors and representative director
Certified seal impression of the company and representative director
Power of attorney, if an agent is used
Foreign investment report certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a supplementary order, respond through IROS within the fixed supplement period, typically 30 days. If registration is suspended for missing fees, pay the assessed registration tax and local surcharge and file the supplement. If the deadline lapses, file an application for restoration or a fresh registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Corporate Tax Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the local district tax office and the Hometax online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the court registration, file a business registration with the National Tax Service through the Hometax portal or the local district tax office. The filing must occur within twenty days of the date the business starts, using the corporate registration certificate, Articles, lease contract, seal certificate, and representative director identity. The tax office will assign a business registration number for VAT, corporate income tax, withholding, and electronic tax invoices. The company must also file the corporation tax commencement report and register the bank account for refunds. A local tax office may ask for proof of office premises and the FSC license status. Once completed, the business registration certificate is used to open operating bank accounts and execute SWIFT payment agreements.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporate Registration from the court registry
Articles of Incorporation
Corporate seal certificate
Foreign investment report certificate
Lease contract for the registered office premises
Identity documents of the representative director
Application for Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service requests additional premises or witness information, submit a lease certificate, building registration extract, and landlord confirmation. If the business registration is wrongly suspended because of the captive licensing status, file a written objection with the local district tax office and provide the FSC license or application receipt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Captive Reinsurance Business Authorization from the Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission (Insurance Business Supervision Bureau) and Financial Supervisory Service (Insurance Examination Bureau).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal authorization application to the Financial Services Commission under Article 4 of the Insurance Business Act. The application must demonstrate a captive reinsurance business plan, restricted underwriting scope limited to group risks, reinsurance arrangements, actuarial reserving, capital adequacy, risk retention, corporate governance, AML manual, parent guarantee, and the proposed compliance officer. The Financial Supervisory Service will conduct a prudential review and may request on-site interviews. If approved, the FSC issues a captive reinsurance business authorization with operating conditions, premium limits, and capital maintenance obligations. The authorization must be obtained before any captive reinsurance contracts are executed. The application should also include the FIU AML registration form for the reporting obligation under the Financial Information Act.
required_dossiers: Application for Insurance Business Authorization for Captive Reinsurance
Certificate of Corporate Registration and Articles of Incorporation
Captive reinsurance business plan and feasibility study
Reinsurance and underwriting policies
Capital adequacy and technical reserve calculations
AML/CTF compliance manual and FIU registration form
Parent company guarantee and audited financial statements
Board resolutions and officer resumes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FSC requires supplementary information or imposes restrictive conditions, file the requested materials within the specified period, usually 14 to 60 days. If approval is denied, the company may file an administrative appeal with the appropriate administrative appeals commission or re-apply after modifying the business plan and capital structure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CTF Registration and Activation of Banking and SWIFT Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit within the Financial Services Commission; authorized foreign exchange banks; SWIFT network.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the captive reinsurance SPV with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit as a reporting company and activate its foreign exchange banking. The compliance officer must file the AML/CTF internal manual, appoint a chief compliance officer, and implement transaction reporting for all SWIFT and underwriting reserve wires. Open or complete the operating bank account by submitting the final business license, captive reinsurance authorization, corporate registration extract, board resolution on signatories, and KYC forms for shareholders and officers. Execute SWIFT payment agreements for premium cessions, underwriting reserve wires, and claims settlements. Bank KYC and AML questionnaires must be completed before transactions are executed. FIU registration filing receipts must be retained for examinations.
required_dossiers: FIU reporting company registration form
AML/CTF internal manual
Compliance officer appointment letter
Captive reinsurance authorization certificate
Bank account opening and KYC documentation
Corporate registration extract and business registration certificate
Board resolution on signatory authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank KYC or FIU registration is delayed, supply the requested shareholder funding source, bank statements, parent audited reports, and beneficial ownership schedule. Provisionally, the bank may permit account opening with restricted transaction limits until the FIU filing receipt is issued.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Commission (Insurance Business Supervision Bureau); Financial Supervisory Service (Insurance Examination Bureau); local municipal government for office occupancy and fire safety review. Physical industrial licensing boards do not apply to ISIC 6512 captive reinsurance because the operation is a financial underwriting SPV.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Captive Reinsurance Business Authorization under Article 4 of the Insurance Business Act of the Republic of Korea, issued as a limited-purpose captive reinsurance SPV license, together with the National Tax Service business registration certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and local municipal environment departments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No Environmental Impact Assessment or Environmental Registration required for an office-based captive reinsurance SPV. The undertaking does not fall within any ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx, or 52xx physical facility category. If the registered office is later converted into a data center or other energy-intensive installation, a separate prior consultation under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act may apply.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial wastewater, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation. Office wastes must be handled under the Waste Management Act with municipal waste disposal receipts; any small battery or electronic item disposal must be through designated recycling channels. No stack or water pollutant discharge threshold applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The lessor and building manager must confirm that the office premises have the Fire Protection System Completion Certificate under the Fire Services Act and pass the periodic Korea Fire Facility Maintenance inspection. Civil defense special permits are not triggered by an office-only captive reinsurance SPV. For occupational safety, the company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act; if it employs ten or more workers, it should satisfy the workplace safety and health plan obligations of the Ministry of Employment and Labor and undergo a basic workplace safety inspection. No structural load or dangerous-chemical clearance is required because the SPV has no manufacturing, assembly, or warehousing operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea and its HomeTax online portal (www.hometax.go.kr); export and customs clearance matters are administered by the Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS electronic customs system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa, the Korean entity must first complete incorporation by registration at the Commercial Registration Office. Within 20 days from the opening of the business, the company must apply for a business registration certificate at the competent local NTS district tax office, either in person or through HomeTax, using the statutory business registration application, articles of incorporation, certificate of company registration, lease or ownership evidence for the registered business place, identity documents of shareholders and directors, and, where applicable, foreign investment documents required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The NTS issues a 10-digit corporate business registration number that serves as both the corporate Tax Identification Number (TIN) and the Value Added Tax (VAT) identification number. A non-resident entity without a fixed Korean place of business that needs to file direct or indirect tax returns is required to appoint a domestic tax representative with an address in Korea before the registration application is processed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch classification election. A Chusik Hoesa is automatically taxed at the entity level on worldwide income under the Corporate Income Tax Act. Qualifying domestic parent-subsidiary corporate groups may elect group taxation for corporate income tax consolidation, but this is a combined filing regime, not an entity classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold applies. Any person individually or jointly carrying on a business, including a captive reinsurance SPV or holding company, is obliged to register for VAT within 20 days of business commencement. A simplified taxpayer regime applies to certain businesses with annual taxable supplies below KRW 80 million, but this changes filing and invoice mechanics and does not exempt registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT invoices issued between registered businesses must be issued as electronic tax invoices through the NTS HomeTax system, and the invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS by the day following the issue date. Korea does not currently operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system for VAT invoices, but UNI-PASS is mandatory for customs export declarations and provides the underlying proof for export VAT zero-rating. Retail and instalment sales also require mandatory cash receipt issuance under the cash receipt system for final consumers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean VAT Act, the export of goods is zero-rated if the goods are actually shipped out of Korea and an export customs declaration is filed with and accepted by the Korea Customs Service. Designated foreign-currency-earning services, including international freight and certain non-resident services, are also zero-rated when supplied to non-resident persons and substantiated with foreign exchange receipts. Offshore digital services supplied by a Korean supplier to a non-resident recipient may qualify for zero-rating if the services are performed or consumed outside Korea and are not classified as VAT-exempt financial, insurance, or reinsurance services. Captive reinsurance and related financial services are generally exempt from Korean VAT rather than zero-rated, which means input VAT recovery on costs directly attributable to such exempt services is restricted unless statutory exceptions apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Customs Declaration approved by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight
Foreign exchange receipt confirmation issued by a licensed foreign exchange bank proving inward remittance or export settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service may jointly audit export declarations and supporting documents for a period of at least five years, extended to ten years in cases of fraudulent omission. Export zero-rating that is unsupported by a valid UNI-PASS export declaration, transport documents, or foreign exchange settlement proof is retroactively reversed, resulting in additional VAT assessment and deemed input tax reversal. Penalties may include an additional tax of up to 40 percent of the amount involved under the Framework Act on National Taxes, and intentional fraudulent conduct may be criminally prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with fines and imprisonment. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the required statutory settlement period may also trigger sanctions under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and can disqualify the supply from zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) as the institutional FX policy executor, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the principal regulator under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA), with operational foreign exchange business supervision delegated to BOK and domestic banks authorised as foreign exchange business institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a broadly liberalised current-account convertibility regime for bona fide trade, reinsurance premiums, claims settlement, dividends and royalties, but capital-account transactions remain subject to a restrictive declaration, notification and statistical-reporting framework under FETA. A captive reinsurance SPV structured as a Chusik Hoesa must ensure every cross-border money movement is classified accurately: inward premium cessions and outward claims payments are current-account service transactions, while an equity injection from a non-resident shareholder is a capital-account foreign direct investment requiring advance MOEF/KOTRA foreign investment notification. There is no mandatory surrender of export/foreign currency proceeds into Korean won, but institutions must submit acquisition-and-payment reports to BOK through their handling foreign exchange bank. Profit remittance is legally unrestricted once an audited balance sheet and board resolution demonstrate distributable reserves; the practical hurdle is not convertibility but the bank's right to demand underlying evidence of the reinsurance arrangement, transfer pricing documentation and the tax residence of every payee before releasing the remittance. The treasury blueprint must therefore maintain an evidentiary file for each wire, including treaty references, actuarial calculations, invoices and settlement vouchers, to satisfy both the commercial bank and BOK audits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The FETA and the Foreign Exchange Transaction Regulations impose no mandatory conversion ratio and no surrender requirement for South Korean residents receiving foreign currency proceeds; export/foreign currency receipts may be held in a foreign currency account at a licensed foreign exchange business institution. However, the exporter or beneficiary must ensure that all proceeds are settled through an authorised Korean foreign exchange bank, reported in the bank's foreign exchange acquisition/payment reporting system, and collected within the contractual trade payment terms. For exports declared to the Korea Customs Service, payment typically must be received within the permissible trade settlement period, commonly five months from the shipping date unless an extension is approved by BOK or the handling bank; overdue collectibles require explanatory documentation and may attract administrative penalties under the Customs Act and FETA.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Weak, and legally barred as a primary treasury rail. An offshore digital EMI without a Korean 'foreign exchange business institution' licence cannot open a domestic KRW operating account or perform FETA-reportable foreign exchange transactions for a Korean entity. FETA restricts foreign exchange business to licenced Korean banks and registered money transfer institutions, so an EMI such as Wise or Revolut Business may only act as an auxiliary remittance conduit through a licenced partner bank. For a captive reinsurance SPV requiring capital verification, FX purpose codes, BOK statistical reporting and documentary settlement of reinsurance treaties, the only viable route is direct onboarding with a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory representative director or an expressly authorised senior officer must normally attend the initial in-branch account opening interview in person with the corporate seal certificate, business registration certificate, foreign investment notification and board resolution. Remote or consular-proxy account opening is not a standard service for a newly formed captive reinsurance company in Korea; if the representative director is a non-resident, the bank may accept an apostilled notarised power of attorney after a video identity verification, but the compliance committee will almost always require a physical or live-video interview with the beneficial owner and will insist on receiving original or certified corporate documents before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity: the captive reinsurance SPV is majority-owned by an offshore holding chain, and the bank cannot identify the natural persons who ultimately control the entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified UBO ownership cascade from the SPV to each natural person owning at least 10%, supported by current registration extracts from each intermediate jurisdiction, passports of all ultimate beneficial owners, tax residence certificates, a signed shareholder registry and an explanatory memorandum from the group treasury confirming no nominee-holding arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-substance red flag: a newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa with minimal paid-in capital intends to book large cross-border radiation from a non-resident parent, leading the bank to suspect a shell conduit.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the captive reinsurance licence or regulatory approval application, executed reinsurance treaty, actuarial underwriting report, loss reserve methodology, independent business plan, evidence of local office or outsourced insurance-management functions, and group audited financial statements demonstrating arm's length pricing and genuine risk transfer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment pattern concern: the SPV receives large premium inflows from abroad and quickly makes outbound claims or dividends, triggering round-tripping or capital-repatriation suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a board-approved treasury policy, full FX transaction history mapped to specific reinsurance contracts, reserve-retention evidence, actuarial support for claims fluctuations, transfer pricing documentation, and the MOEF/KOTRA foreign investment registration certificate showing the permitted use of injected capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/high-risk counterparty exposure: ceding insurers or insured corporate group subsidiaries operate in jurisdictions subject to international sanctions or heightened money-laundering screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver end-to-end sanctions and PEP screening results for all ceding insurers, reinsured group entities and beneficiaries; source-of-funds evidence for premium wires; contractual ML/TF warranties and audit rights; and a claims register showing the underlying policy numbers, insured property descriptions and legal beneficiary registration details.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The non-resident investor must complete the foreign direct investment notification with MOEF/KOTRA before moving funds, then route a clean SWIFT MT103 from the investor's overseas bank to the SPV's designated capital account at a Korean Tier-1 bank, using the direct-investment FX purpose code and clearly referencing the foreign investment registration number. Upon receipt, the Korean bank verifies the remittance against the registered capital, issues a foreign exchange bank handling certificate, credits the Capital Escrow Account or Basic Operational Currency Account, and the capital verification is evidenced by an audited balance sheet or certified bank confirmation. A separate MT103, with a different invoice or contract reference, must be used for premium income or operating disbursements so that capital-account and current-account flows are not commingled for BOK statistical reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For foreign reinsurance claims and premium cessions to non-resident counterparties, the preferred clearing rail is a priority SWIFT MT103 message through the SPV's Korean foreign exchange bank, with each wire carrying the exact treaty or claim number and the relevant FETA current-account purpose code. Where a fronting insurer or cedant requires secured recoverables, use a Commercial Letter of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700, with presentation of claims documents, loss settlement certificates and signed bordereaux; for lower-value counterparties, Documentary Collections are acceptable if the bank has already cleared the counterparty's standing KYC profile. The treasury must pre-file copies of reinsurance agreements, claim calculation sheets and beneficiary tax identifications so that the bank does not freeze high-frequency outbound payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore Korean won forward contracts booked with a domestic Tier-1 bank and limited to authentic reinsurance premium, claims or capital flow hedging
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) allowed only where the SPV has documented KRW exposure and settles against a recognised fixing rate
Cross-currency swaps permitted only for the direct investment and borrowing related principal and interest flows, not for speculative arbitrage
Plain vanilla currency options acceptable if the notional amount is fully supported by expected premium receipts or known claims liabilities

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (including reconciliation schedules and audited financial statements attachment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the third month after fiscal year-end (March 31 for a December 31 year-end); automatic one-month extension to April 30 where the company is externally audited or where the return is prepared by a certified tax accountant.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 20% of assessed tax for fraudulent understatement, 10% general non-filing penalty, plus statutory underpayment interest of 1.2% per month; repeated non-filing for two consecutive years is an administrative forfeiture trigger enabling the NTS to seek compulsory collection and a court order for strike-off of the corporate registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surtax at 10% of national corporate income tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Taxation Authority (city/province) via the local electronic tax system with the NTS remittance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory deadline as the corporate income tax return (March 31 or April 30 if the underlying national return is extended).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment and non-filing penalty of 10% of unpaid local tax plus statutory monthly interest of 0.75%; persistent non-payment triggers a local tax lien and administrative strike-off action against the captive SPV's registered seat.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent auditor's financial statements report filed through the FSS DART system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System (DART)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end (March 31 for December 31 year-end), following approval of the financial statements by the annual shareholders' meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under the External Audit Act, failure to submit is punishable by an administrative fine of up to KRW 30 million (approx. USD 22,000); issuing false audited opinions results in criminal liability for the directors and external auditor; repeat violations can lead to court-ordered dissolution of the reinsurance SPV.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual insurance supervision report for the captive reinsurance SPV (solvency margin certificate, technical reserve computation, and reinsurance asset coverage schedule)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / Financial Services Commission (FSC) Insurance Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the second month after the fiscal year-end (February 28/29 for December 31 year-end), unless the FSS approves a specific extension for licensed special-purpose financial entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty of up to KRW 50 million (approx. USD 37,000) for omission or false material statements; non-submission triggers FSC corrective orders including capital supplementation, suspension of underwriting, and final license revocation for the captive reinsurer.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Court registration of corporate constitutional changes and shareholder ledger updates (directors, registered office, share transfers, charges, and other registrable matters)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate Registration Section, Court Registry of the Republic of Korea (accessible through the ORDE online registration portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 calendar days (2 weeks) of any corporate change; for beneficial share transfers, the share register must be updated within the same 14-day window, with no separate annual no-change filing required for the court registry if no change occurs.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 5 million (approx. USD 3,700) against the responsible officer for late registration; continuous and willful non-compliance may lead the court to issue an ex officio dissolution registration, effectively canceling the Chusik Hoesa's legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership and substantial shareholder confirmation for the regulated captive reinsurer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and, as applicable, the FSC Insurance Supervisor
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the annual insurance supervision report by February 28/29 for December year-end; any change of direct or indirect shareholding equal to or above 4.99% must be reported within 30 days of completion of the transaction.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or inaccurate UBO confirmation triggers an administrative penalty up to KRW 20 million (approx. USD 14,700) and is treated as an AML governance deficiency; recurrence may result in suspension of the insurance license and a mandated divestiture order.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is required under Article 2 of the Korean External Audit Act for any enterprise that (i) is listed on a Korean exchange, or (ii) has total assets equal to or exceeding KRW 12,000,000,000 (approximately USD 9,000,000) as at the end of the preceding fiscal year. In addition, under the Korean Insurance Business Act and FSC regulations, all licensed insurance and reinsurance companies—including a captive reinsurance SPV classified under ISIC 6512/NAICS 524130—are subject to a full external audit by a registered certified public accountant irrespective of asset size. The audit must cover solvency margin, technical reserves, inter-company reinsurance balances, and compliance with IFRS 17 disclosure requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards, as designated by the Korean Accounting Standards Board) is mandatory for regulated insurance and reinsurance carriers. A captive reinsurance SPV must apply K-IFRS 9 Financial Instruments, K-IFRS 17 Insurance Contracts, and the incremental insurance-specific disclosure requirements issued by the FSS. K-SME GAAP is not permitted for licensed insurance entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: For a private unlisted Korean Chusik Hoesa, the law does not impose a separate standalone annual UBO return for ordinary no-change years; however, the company is required to maintain a current shareholder ledger and, for a licensed captive reinsurer, to provide a UBO confirmation to KoFIU as part of the annual insurance supervision report. Any beneficial ownership change of 4.99% or more of the issued shares must be reported to KoFIU within 30 days of the transaction, and the corporate registry change must be filed with the court registration office within 14 days. The board must keep the substantial-shareholder register available at the registered office and present it at the annual shareholders' meeting.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 2,500 per year for registered agent services, office maintenance, and annual filing facilitation by a corporate secretarial or legal-services firm in Seoul or a regional financial hub.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - USD 60,000 per year for a licensed Korean CPA firm (e.g., Samil PwC, Samjong KPMG, or MVP equivalent) to conduct the statutory audit of the captive reinsurance entity and submit the certified report to the FSS.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: National corporate income tax progressive brackets: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on taxable income over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 21% on taxable income over KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion; 24% on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion. A 10% local corporate income tax surcharge applies to national corporate tax, producing combined effective rates of 9.9%, 20.9%, 23.1%, and 26.4% respectively. A non-resident Chusik Hoesa with a Korean domestic business place is taxed on Korean-source profits at these same rates.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general patent box for captive reinsurance. Limited incentives under the Special Tax Reduction Control Act: (1) R&D tax credits for qualifying insurance/regTech and actuarial analytics; (2) 50% corporate tax reduction for 5-7 years for eligible new-growth/corporate headquarters foreign investments and certain Free Economic Zone / International Free Economic Zone projects; (3) tax amortization of acquired intangible assets; (4) NOL carryforward of 10 years with annual deduction caps, generally 60% of taxable income for large corporations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return for a foreign corporation's domestic business place, including the official corporate income tax return schedules and the foreign corporation adjustment statements, filed electronically through the Korean National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, on a fiscal-year basis; a short-period return is due upon establishment, liquidation, or closure of a Korean business place, and provisional corporate tax installments are payable mid-year with final annual reconciliation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 3 months from the last day of the taxable fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, the return is due by March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension to April 30 for calendar-year taxpayers may be granted by filing an extension request through HomeTax with book-closing and audit-supporting documents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All operating and non-operating revenue of the Korean captive reinsurance SPV, including earned reinsurance premiums, sub-commission income, investment income from reserves, interest, dividends, and exchange gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report full accrual-basis revenue under K-IFRS or Korean GAAP as booked. Reconcile to the segregated reinsurance reserve accounts; do not net ceding commissions against premium revenue. If part of premium is received offshore for Korean underwriting risk, include Korean allocable premium and disclose the allocation method in the international-transaction attachments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Items excluded from the tax base under the Corporate Tax Act, such as certain qualified dividend income, capital contributions, and income expressly exempt by tax treaty where Korea is not the source state.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Narrowly apply. In a captive reinsurance SPV, the most common non-taxable items are refunds of returned capital contributions, not underwriting income. For treaty-exempt income, attach the relevant treaty article, Tax Residency Certificate, and risk-allocation analysis; the NTS will reclassify income as taxable if the SPV merely books premiums without Korean core income-generating activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Gross income after non-taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The Korean-source gross income before expense deductions, equal to Box 1 minus Box 2.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that premium income is sourced to Korea when the insured risk is located in Korea. If the SPV under-bills a related offshore reinsurer, the NTS may calculate constructive premium income; use the same premium allocation method as the reinsurance contract and the international-transaction report.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss reserve additions, unearned premium reserve, acquisition commissions, claims paid, actuarial fees, professional services, salaries, depreciation, and other ordinary and necessary business expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses attributable to the Korean business are deductible if supported by proper invoices and recognized under Korean tax law. Premiums paid to a non-resident fronting reinsurer must satisfy the arm's length standard and economic substance; excessive ceding commissions or unjustified loss reserves are adjusted. Add back expenses directly connected to tax-exempt income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory non-deductible items: penalties, fines, corporate income tax, local income tax, excess entertainment, excess retirement reserves, and expenses without proper withholding or documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign affiliates, such as service fees or management fees that duplicate Korean functions, must be added back if no actual services or risk management are performed. Also add back interest on excessive related-party debt under the Korean thin-capitalization rules, currently 2:1 debt-to-equity for domestic foreign-controlled corporations and 6:1 for financial institutions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Taxable income before loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income minus deductible expenses plus non-deductible additions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-controlled captive, this amount must be consistent with the OECD transfer-pricing adjustments and the Korean International Tax Adjustment Act reports. A loss here is respected only if the SPV bears real underwriting risk; otherwise the NTS may disregard the loss and reattribute profit to the offshore parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Korean net operating loss deductions from available carried-forward tax losses, subject to the statutory carryforward period and annual deduction limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2019, the carryforward period is 10 years. For SPVs, a carried-forward loss may be denied or reduced if a merger, stock transfer, or change of business purpose occurred without a bona fide business purpose under the anti-abuse rule. Attach the separate schedule with year-by-year loss computations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Final taxable income after all adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The final amount taxed at progressive national corporate rates, after transfer-pricing adjustments, tax-holiday deductions, reserve re-additions, and all out-of-book tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The final tax base must be reported in KRW and must equal the amount reflected in the audited financial statements after tax reconciliation. Any upward transfer-pricing adjustment made by the NTS must be included; self-initiated TP adjustments must be disclosed on the international-transaction attachments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 - National corporate income tax and local income tax surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National tax at the 9%/19%/21%/24% brackets and local corporate income tax at 10% of the national tax computed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No treaty rate reduction applies to the SPV's own net taxable income. Any foreign home-state tax credit must be claimed under Korean tax law, not under the withholding regime, and must be evidenced by foreign-tax certificates and a treaty foreign-tax-credit schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Tax credits and special deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, early-filing penalty relief, R&D credits, and other statutory credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A captive reinsurance SPV claiming foreign tax credit for taxes paid to the parent jurisdiction must attach the treaty foreign-tax-credit calculation and demonstrate that the income is also taxable in Korea. No credit is allowed for taxes saved by a treaty exemption or for taxes paid on income that is not sourced in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11 - Total tax payable after credits and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final national and local corporate income tax payable to the NTS after provisional payments, credits, and withholding offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If provisional payments exceed total liability, claim a refund; if less, remit the balance by the statutory due date. Branch remittance tax is reported separately, not in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 12 - Branch remittance tax / non-resident branch profit distribution declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 20% branch remittance tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge on amounts distributed or deemed distributed to a foreign head office out of after-tax Korean-source profits, unless reduced by an applicable tax treaty.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete this schedule when the SPV remits profits to its foreign parent or when a portion of PE profits is attributed to the head office. Reinvested profits retained in Korea and actually used in the business are exempt; artificial loans or capital drops to the head office are recharacterized as remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13 - International transaction report and transfer-pricing attachments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule reporting all cross-border related-party transactions, including reinsurance premiums, commissions, claims, expenses, interest, and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for foreign-controlled SPVs with overseas related-party transactions; attach the Transfer Pricing Local File/Master File when applicable. State the selected transfer-pricing method, usually CUP for facultative reinsurance or TNMM for a captive service/holding function, together with the benchmark study and financial data, all in KRW.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax, plus daily late-payment surcharges of 0.03% per day on overdue amounts. Negligent underreporting generally draws an additional tax of 10% of the underpaid tax; intentional or false documentation can raise the penalty to 30-40%. Failure to submit transfer-pricing documentation or international-transaction reports triggers separate statutory penalty taxes. Willful evasion, fraudulent returns, or abuse of treaty relief is referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to 5 times the tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% of gross dividend amount paid by the Chusik Hoesa to a non-resident shareholder, composed of 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge. Bilateral DTA relief commonly reduces this rate to 5-15%, with many Korean treaties providing 10% for a direct corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the shares.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced or zero DTA withholding rate, the non-resident shareholder or lender must submit to the Korean payor before payment: (1) a Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority; (2) a completed Application for Tax Exemption or Reduction under Tax Treaty, filed with the NTS; (3) a beneficial ownership statement proving the recipient is the actual owner of the dividend and is not a conduit; (4) evidence of corporate status and shareholding percentage; and (5) a permanent establishment non-attachment declaration confirming the income is not effectively connected with a Korean PE or fixed base. If treaty relief is not obtained before the withholding date, the non-resident recipient may apply for a refund within the applicable Korean tax-procedure statute of limitations, generally within 5 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding on outbound interest and royalties is 22% combined, being 20% national tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge. Treaty rates generally range from 10% to 15% for interest and 10% to 20% for royalties, depending on the bilateral convention and the character of the intellectual property. Interest and royalties paid to a foreign related party still require beneficial ownership substantiation and satisfaction of the OECD MLI principal purpose test; the Korean payer is liable for penalties if it fails to withhold, even if the recipient later obtains a treaty refund.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under the Korean International Tax Adjustment Act and its Enforcement Decree, a taxpayer engaged in foreign-related-party transactions must prepare and, upon NTS request, submit contemporaneous Local File and Master File documentation when total foreign-related transactions for the fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 10 billion. International-transaction reports are required at lower thresholds, generally any cross-border related-party transaction of at least KRW 100 million, and a tax-haven counterparty or offshore captive reinsurance SPV can trigger audit scrutiny even below KRW 10 billion.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (comparable uncontrolled price) for fronting reinsurance rates and commissions
Resale price method for distribution-type flows
Cost plus method for management or claims-handling services
TNMM (transactional net margin method) for captive reinsurance performing routine functions
Profit split method for integrated reinsurance shared-risk arrangements
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations of the Gulf Cooperation Council type, but the NTS applies substantive anti-abuse doctrines and CFC rules. The captive SPV's underwriting, actuarial, investment-management, risk-absorption, reserve-setting, and claims-approval functions must be genuinely performed by Korean personnel using adequate office, IT systems, and insurance licenses. The Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14 substance-over-form doctrine, the International Tax Adjustment Act Article 17 CFC regime, and the OECD MLI principal purpose test permit the NTS to recharacterize the SPV, deny treaty benefits, and impute income to the Korean controlling shareholder if core income-generating activities are performed outside Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed captive insurance and sham reinsurance SPV with corporate-veil piercing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SPV is incorporated as a Chusik Hoesa and presented as a captive reinsurance vehicle but has no Korean Insurance Business Act authorization, no licensed officers or qualified actuaries, no actual underwriting or claim-adjudication functions in Korea, and executes circular reinsurance contracts solely to shift premiums and profits to a tax-favored offshore affiliate. It maintains no meaningful risk capital, and board decisions are rubber-stamped by the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed insurance business is criminally sanctionable under the Korean Insurance Business Act with imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to KRW 200 million, or both. The NTS will deny deductions, apply 30-40% additional tax for intentionally false returns, and disregard the sham contracts under the Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto directors who approved the sham contracts are jointly and severally liable for damages to the company and third parties under Korean Commercial Act Articles 389(3) and 401. The NTS may pursue director assets where the corporation is a mere conduit, impose overseas travel bans, attach personal assets, and refer directors for criminal prosecution with imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Aggressive transfer pricing, profit shifting, and false transfer-pricing documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SPV books related-party reinsurance premiums and ceding commissions that are not supported by transactional comparables: it assumes 100% of the group's actuarial risk while earning only a guaranteed 1% commission; premium flows are structured to move Korean underwriting profit offshore; loss reserves are documented by a one-page parent-CFO memo; and the SPV fails to prepare or files false Local File and Master File documentation despite KRW 10 billion or more in cross-border related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The NTS may adjust taxable income under the International Tax Adjustment Act, impose documentation penalties for missing TP files, apply 10-30% additional tax on false reporting, and charge daily late-payment surcharges. Criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act include imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines of up to 5 times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The CFO, CEO, TP-document preparers, and de facto controllers who participate in intentional evasion are jointly liable for unpaid corporate taxes when the SPV is a shell. Directors may face civil liability under Korean Commercial Act Article 401, personal fines, confiscation of profits transferred abroad, and an NTS departure-prevention order blocking international travel until the tax liabilities are satisfied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Outbound withholding tax evasion and abusive treaty relief or dividend stripping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SPV pays dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident parent without withholding the statutory 22% tax, or claims a zero or reduced DTA rate using a photocopied Tax Residency Certificate while the foreign shareholder is a no-substance conduit in a treaty jurisdiction, or disguises profit repatriation as deductible interest on a 6:1 debt-to-equity related-party loan instead of declared dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer is liable for the unpaid withholding tax, daily 0.03% delinquency surcharge, and a withholding non-compliance penalty of generally 10% of the unwithheld amount, with aggravated rates for intentional non-withholding. False treaty-benefit claims may trigger reassessment and 30-40% additional tax; willful evasion through a captive SPV is prosecutable under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to 5 times the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly direct the payment without withholding are personally liable for the withheld tax and penalties under the Korean responsible-management liability rule. Courts may pierce the corporate veil and order the foreign parent and its appointed Korean directors to compensate the company's unpaid tax. In flagrant cases, directors are blacklisted, prohibited from leaving Korea, and may face imprisonment of up to 5 years, in addition to civil damages under Korean Commercial Act Article 401.
